subject: Prefix warmup & fallback rehearsal: edge priming log
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acuitycloud.com>, DevOps Team <devops@acuitycloud.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Prefix warmup & fallback rehearsal: edge priming log

Hi Sara / Acuity Ops team —

Thanks for booking today's priming window. High-level plan and asks below so we can stay in the same lane: 

- Objective: perform prefix warmup (synthetic prefix announcements + KV cache priming) and validate fallback behavior with a live traffic canary for 30 minutes.
- Runbook: use the linked runbook (see link in thread) and follow the exact sequence under "priming -> fallback rehearsal".
- Measurables: average p95 tail latency, token throughput, and successful KV cache hits by client attempt ID.
- Expected impacts: short tail-period BGP churn (~2min) when announcing test prefixes; no user-facing downtime planned.

Mina and Marcus will coordinate the KV priming steps and watch for any abnormal error rates in the console. Please confirm you can accept the advertised prefixes and that your transit fabric will honor the community tags we discussed (no prep change required at your end).

If you see anything that looks like partial routing leakage, abort with the stop command in the runbook and we will immediately withdraw test advertisements.

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-cache-priming.log.txt (attached after rehearsal)

From: Sara Patel <sara@acuitycloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acuitycloud.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prefix warmup & fallback rehearsal: edge priming log

Jonas — thanks for the clear plan. We can take the window. A couple quick questions before we start: 

1) Can you paste the exact prefixes and AS-paths you'll announce so our edge team can validate filters?
2) We'll want the runbook steps as a quick PDF for our incident room — can you attach the specific cut we should follow (priming -> failover rehearsal).

We are good to proceed as long as: prefixes are in the test pool, route target communities are the same as prior rehearsals, and the failover stop command is explicit.

—Sara
Director, Cloud Ops
AcuityCloud

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acuitycloud.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prefix warmup & fallback rehearsal: edge priming log

Sara — attaching the trimmed runbook PDF (fallback-rehearsal-notes.pdf) and a short log from our staging priming run. Key details below: 

- Test prefixes: 198.51.100.0/24, 198.51.101.0/24 (announce only to test transit).
- AS-path: we will prepend once: {Redwood-AS 65040} -> community: no-export,test:1001
- Stop command (if you see leakage): runbook section 4.2, command: 
  ./redwood-ctl withdrawal --prefix 198.51.100.0/24 --immediate

KV priming sequence (summary):
1) Execute priming lambda: POST https://priming.redwood.ai/priming?k=acuity-test
2) Monitor console: /metrics/kv/hit-rate (expect >80% after warmup)
3) Gradual canary traffic: 1% -> 10% -> 30% over 10 minute windows

We also captured a short snippet from the staging KV log; saved as kv-cache-priming.log.txt (attached). Sample log extract: 
[10:01:12] priming: key=tenant-acuity:50: lookups=1200 hits=980 hit_rate=81.6%

I'll be on the bridge for the first two phases and will escalate to Marcus for fallback execution if we need to exercise the roll-back.

—Mina
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fallback-rehearsal-notes.pdf, kv-cache-priming.log.txt

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara@acuitycloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prefix warmup & fallback rehearsal: edge priming log

Quick note from the rehearsal: we ran the fallback path on the staging mirror at 11:20 and saw the following behavior:

- Failover trigger: synthetic prefix withdraw at t=0, upstream re-route seen at t=18s, client reconnects at t=21s.
- Telemetry: p99 spiked from 420ms -> 1.2s for ~45s, then returned to baseline.

Recommendation: during production priming, set canary policy to 5% for the first 15 minutes to limit exposure and confirm KV hit-rate >85% before stepping to 20%. If everything looks green at the 20% window, proceed to 50% for final validation.

Operational checklist items I adjusted in the runbook (see attached PDF): 
- Add explicit BGP observation step (verify AS-path and community tags).
- Add transit filter verification: ensure no-export applied on test prefixes.
- Add a post-prime latency sample capture and attach to ticket OPS-3271.

Laura — can you capture a short post-run observability snapshot (Console -> per-route latencies) and drop into the Jira ticket?

—Marcus
Senior SRE Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acuitycloud.com>, DevOps Team <devops@acuitycloud.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prefix warmup & fallback rehearsal: edge priming log

Thanks everyone — nice execution. Short readout / final state: 

- Go/no-go: GO for production priming tomorrow 09:00 PST with the adjusted canary schedule (5% -> 20% -> 50%).
- Owners: Acuity to accept prefixes + watch for any route leakage; Redwood to drive priming and fallback if needed (Mina on first hour, Marcus on fallback).
- Post-run artifacts: Mina to upload full priming log (kv-cache-priming.log.txt) and Marcus to attach observability snapshot to OPS-3271.
- Follow-ups: if p99 > 1s for more than 2 consecutive minutes during any step, abort and open a war room.

I'll send the calendar invite for tomorrow's 09:00 window and include the runbook link and emergency stop CLI in the invite body. Good work — closing this rehearsal thread.

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
